body.statement: For every \(r\ge C\max\{R_n^{\mathrm{NP}},r_G,r_F\}\), can \(H_{\mathrm{pair\mbox{-}lift}}\) construct a family \(\{Q_t:t\in\mathcal G_r\}\) such that \(\sup_{D_n\sim_1D_n'}|Q_t(D_n)-Q_t(D_n')|\le1\) for every \(t\) and \(\mathfrak W_r(Q)\le C'\), with \(C'\) independent of every finite nuisance sieve, using the same sample size \(n\)?
body.justification: This is the open step from the proved signed-family pair test to a symbolic full-class private upper frontier.
body.gap: Birgé-style composite tests and Asi et al.'s Section 4 T-mechanism do not establish a nuisance-independent second-order projection certificate for arbitrary dependent least-favorable CATE mixtures.
body.consumer: A positive answer and Proposition 3 yield \(R_{n,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{DP}}\le C\max\{R_n^{\mathrm{NP}},r_G,r_F\}\); a negative answer identifies a privacy obstruction beyond the signed pair witness.
